pathophysiology.summary: Noisy, bubbly breathing may occur in around 70% of patients in the terminal phase. Evidence for drug treatment is limited, but anticholinergics are established practice to reduce further secretions. Hyoscine butylbromide and glycopyrronium do not usually cause drowsiness, confusion or paradoxical excitation because they do not cross the blood-brain barrier.

clinicalManagement.title: Explain and reassure
actions: Explain to relatives and carers; this is paramount.

clinicalManagement.title: Non-drug measures
actions: Reposition in high side-lying with head tilted; consider a fan; gentle suction if saliva pools.

clinicalManagement.title: Subcutaneous stat or as-needed dose
actions: Hyoscine butylbromide 20 mg or glycopyrronium 200 micrograms subcutaneously.

clinicalManagement.title: Syringe driver
actions: Hyoscine butylbromide 60 to 120 mg or glycopyrronium 600 to 1,200 micrograms over 24 hours.

clinicalManagement.title: Adjust in renal impairment
actions: Glycopyrronium 400 to 800 micrograms over 24 hours in mild to moderate impairment; the page notes the usual maximum may be applied at end of life.
